extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians/geometers or advanced students studying classical constructions of conic sections and orbital trajectories
extracted.subtask_description: Classical Euclidean constructions and criteria for describing conic-section trajectories (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) from given data: umbilici (foci), vertices, latus rectum, given points and tangents, and related locus constructions. Includes lemmas that reduce or transform problems and methods to test tangency/membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Velocity determines conic species
rubrics_metrics.description: If the body's velocity at a given point is less than a critical value (related to the latus rectum and distances), the resulting trajectoria is an ellipse; if it equals the critical value, the trajectoria is a parabola (with infinite length of PH); if it exceeds the critical value the trajectoria is a hyperbola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the body's speed in the vertex with the threshold given by the geometry (relations involving the latus rectum L and distances SP, KP, PH). The sign of PH (added or subtracted from SP) distinguishes ellipse (PH + SP), parabola (PH makes length infinite), and hyperbola (PH − SP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: locating the other umbilicus from vertex, latus rectum, and one umbilicus
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a conic with principal vertex D, latus rectum L, and one umbilicus S, the other umbilicus H is found by taking DH to DS as latus rectum to the difference between latus rectum and 4·DS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the proportion SP + PH : PH = 2 SP : L (specialized in the Corollary) leading to DS:DH = 4·DS − L : L after algebraic manipulation; this yields the position of H relative to S and D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: quick orbit determination from velocity at principal vertex
rubrics_metrics.description: If the body's velocity at the principal vertex D is given, the orbit may be obtained rapidly by taking the latus rectum to twice the distance DS in the duplicate (squared) ratio of the given velocity to the circular velocity at distance DS; then find DH:DS as latus rectum to its difference with 4·DS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the velocity ratio squared to scale the latus rectum vs. doubled DS, then use the same construction as in Corollary 1 to fix the other umbilicus and thus the conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: composition of impulsive motion determines subsequent orbit
rubrics_metrics.description: If a body moving in any conic section receives an arbitrary impulsive velocity, the resulting orbit after the impulse can be determined by composing the original motion with the motion that the impulse alone would generate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add vectorially the existing motion and the impulse-generated motion to obtain the resultant motion; the new orbit is the conic having those motion-data with the same geometric construction rules applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: small continuous perturbations estimated from discrete impulses
rubrics_metrics.description: If a body is continually perturbed by a small external force, the new course can be approximated by collecting the finite changes induced at certain points and using series analogy to estimate continuous changes at intermediate points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat continuous perturbations as the limit of many small impulses; calculate the discrete changes at sample points and use series/analogy to interpolate to the continuous case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XV (tangency test via two lines to a point)
rubrics_metrics.description: From two umbilici S, H to any third point V draw lines SV and HV; if one of these equals the transverse axis of the figure and the other is bisected by a perpendicular TR (from the given tangent) at T, then that perpendicular TR touches the conic; conversely, if TR is tangent then VH equals the axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use equalities TS = TV and symmetry of triangles (TS = TV implies equal angles TRS and TRV) to deduce tangency; conversely tangency yields the equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XVIII Prob. X — construct ellipse/hyperbola through point and tangent given umbilicus and transverse axis
rubrics_metrics.description: Given common umbilicus S, axis transverse length AB, a point P through which the trajectoria must pass, and a tangent line TR to be contacted: with centre P and radius AB − SP (for ellipse) or AB + SP (for hyperbola) describe a circle HG; drop perpendicular ST to TR and extend to V so TV = ST; with centre V and radius AB describe circle FH. The intersection H of the two circles together with umbilici S, H and the given axis describe the trajectoria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction reduces to drawing two circles (centers P and V) with radii determined by AB and SP (adding or subtracting depending on ellipse/hyperbola), then the common intersection yields the second umbilicus H; Lemma XV guarantees tangency at TR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XIX Prob. XI — construct parabola through point and tangent given umbilicus
rubrics_metrics.description: Given umbilicus S, a point P and a tangent TR: with centre P and radius PS describe circle FG; from S to TR drop perpendicular ST and extend to V so TV = ST. If a second circle (from another point or tangent) is needed, construct similarly. Draw line FI which is tangent to the two circles; from FI drop perpendicular SI, bisect it at K, and with axis SK the parabola with vertex K is described; it passes through P and is tangent to TR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tangency follows from equal right angles and equal segments ST and TV; the bisector step finds the parabola's vertex because of equal SK and IK and equal SP and FP relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XX Prob. XII Case 1 — construct trajectoria of given species through two points
rubrics_metrics.description: Given umbilicus S and desired trajectoria species (ratio of transverse axis to umbilic distance), and two points B, C through which the trajectoria must pass: take KB:BS and LC:CS in that species-ratio; with centres B, C and radii BK and CL describe two circles; let KL be the common tangent touching them at K and L; drop perpendicular SG to KL and cut in A and a so that SA:AG and Sa:aG equal SB:BK etc. The axis Aa with vertices A and a describes the trajectoria of the given species passing through B and C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce the species constraint to proportional construction of distances from B and C, then construct circles and tangent, and derive the axis by perpendiculars from the umbilicus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XX Prob. XII Case 2 — construct trajectoria given two tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: Given umbilicus S and two tangents TR and tr to be contacted: from S drop perpendiculars ST and St to the two tangents and extend to V and v so TV = TS and tv = ts; bisect Vv at O and erect perpendicular OH; cut the infinite extension of VS in points K and k so that VK:KS and Vk:kS match the required transverse-axis to umbilici-distance ratio. The circle on diameter Kk that meets the produced line VR at H yields the second umbilicus; with S,H and axis VH the trajectoria is described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constructs the required umbilici by symmetry and proportional division of VS given the species ratio; Lemma XV ensures tangency to the given lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XX Prob. XII Case 3 — construct trajectoria tangent at a given point
rubrics_metrics.description: Given umbilicus S and a tangent TR that the trajectoria must touch at a given point R: drop ST to TR and extend to V so TV = ST. Join VR and cut the infinite extension VS in K and k so VK:SK and Vk:Sk equal the required axis-to-umbilic distance ratio (as for ellipse construction). Describe circle on Kk; its intersection with VR gives H, and with S,H and the given axis the trajectoria is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essentially a specialization of Case 2 where one tangent and a point of contact are given; use proportional cutting on VS and circle intersection to locate the other umbilicus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XX Prob. XII Case 4 — construct trajectoria similar to a given figure
rubrics_metrics.description: Given umbilicus S and a trajectoria similar in species to a given figure apb with transverse axis ab and umbilici s,h: drop perpendicular ST to the given tangent TR and extend to V so TV = ST; form angles VSP and SVP equal to given reference angles (hsq, shq) and construct a circle (center q) with interval to ab proportional to SP:VS to locate a corresponding point p. By proportion and similarity transfer, construct H such that VH equals ab and the new trajectoria is similar and passes through the required point P and touches TR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use similarity of triangles and proportional construction to map a known conic figure to one with the given umbilicus and tangency/point constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XVI — locating a point from three distance-differences using hyperbolae
rubrics_metrics.description: Given three fixed points A,B,C and a fourth point Z to be found such that differences of linear distances AZ, BZ (or their differences) are given or zero: Z lies on a hyperbola having A and B as umbilici with transverse axis equal to the given difference. Construct three such hyperbolae (pairwise) and intersect their corresponding loci; the intersection of two such loci gives Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each pair of given base points construct a hyperbola with prescribed difference of distances to yield a locus for Z; intersecting two such loci gives the fourth point. Special symmetric cases (equal differences) reduce to perpendicular bisector or circle centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXI Prob. XIII — finding the other umbilicus from umbilicus, point, and tangent
rubrics_metrics.description: Given umbilicus S, a point P through which the trajectoria passes, and tangent TR to be contacted, drop ST perpendicular to TR and extend to Y so TY = ST; then YH equals the transverse axis. Joining SP and HP shows SP is the difference between HP and the axis; repeating for other given tangents/points yields lines YH or PH from which the other umbilicus H is found; with the umbilici and axis, the trajectoria is then determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert each given tangent/point into a constraint (a line YH or PH) that either equals an axis or differs by a given amount; use Lemma XVI to solve for H by intersection of such lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium: expedited construction when three points are given
rubrics_metrics.description: If three points B,C,D are given, construct lines BC and CD and extend them to E and F so that EB:EC = SB:SC and FC:FD = SC:SD. Draw normals from E F and take parallels and proportional segments as described to produce a vertex A and axis Aa; depending on the size of GA relative to AS the trajectoria will be ellipse, parabola or hyperbola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportional extension and perpendicular construction from the three given points to produce the axis and vertex directly; this yields a quicker construction for the common case of three prescribed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XVII — product-of-segments proportionality in trapezium
rubrics_metrics.description: If from a given point P four lines PQ, PR, PS, PT are drawn to the four sides of a trapezium ABCD at given angles (each to its corresponding side), then the rectangle PQ × PR is to PS × PT in a given ratio (determined by the trapezium and P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proportionality follows by reducing to cases where pairs of sides are parallel and applying properties of rectangles formed with equal differences; the lemma is a tool to relate segment-products to membership in a conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XVIII — tangency criterion via rectangle-product ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: With the same setup as Lemma XVII, if PQ×PR is to PS×PT in a given ratio, then the point P lies on (i.e., tangents) the conic section inscribed about the trapezium. Conversely, if P is on the conic then the product ratio holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a test: compute the products of pairs of segments from P to the trapezium sides (or construct them geometrically); equality with the required ratio implies P is on the intended conic, and conversely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XIX — determine point producing given rectangle-product ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Given four position lines AB, CD, AC, BD and the requirement that PQ×PR : PS×PT have a given ratio, one may select any line AH in which P is to lie, use known angular data to derive ratios PQ:PA and PA:PS and hence PQ:PS; subtracting from the given overall product ratio yields PR:PT; combining with the given ratios PI:PR and PT:PH locates P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit method to compute the unknown point P by reducing the product condition to simpler proportional relations along a chosen line and then solving sequentially for the required segment ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XX — parallelogram tangent-abscissa proportionality
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram ASPQ (with opposite vertices A,P) touches a conic in A and P and its two infinitely produced sides AQ, AS meet the conic again in B, C; from those meeting points draw lines to any fifth point D and meet the parallels PS,PQ at T and R — then the abscissa parts PR and PT are to each other in a given ratio. Conversely, if PR and PT are in the given ratio then the point D touches the conic through the four points A,B,P,C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a way to detect or enforce tangency by measuring abscissa parts in a parallelogram construction; use similarity and previous lemmas to reduce to product-of-rectangles relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXI — locus from intersections of families of lines (moving poles)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two movable infinite lines BM and CM rotate about fixed poles B and C producing a variable intersection M lying on a fixed position line MN, and if two other infinite lines BD and CD are drawn through B and C making specific given angles with BM and CM, then the intersection D of BD and CD describes a conic section. Conversely, if BD and CD describe a conic through B,C,A then the intersection D moves accordingly and the moving pole intersection M traces a fixed line MN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lemma provides a method to generate/realize conic loci by coupling two rotating rays about fixed poles and then constructing the angular lines BD, CD; the intersections of these latter lines trace the conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXII Prob. XIV — construct trajectoria through five given points
rubrics_metrics.description: Given five points A,B,C,D,P, choose any two to be treated as poles B,C and construct parallels TPS and PRQ through them with the given angular data, then through the fifth point D draw two infinite lines BDT and CRD meeting TPS and PRQ in T and R; proportionally cut segments Pt, Pr of PT, PR and let the lines through the poles B,C across those proportional points meet at d; the limit as the auxiliary choices vanish gives the trajectoria through the five points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the required auxiliary parallels and proportional cuts to create a point d on the desired conic (Lemma XX used). The second alternative (rotating-limb construction) gives a mechanical way to trace the conic by rotating limbs about poles and recording intersections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXIII Prob. XV — construct trajectoria through four points and a tangent
rubrics_metrics.description: Given tangent HB with contact point B and three other points C,D,P: form parallelogram BSPQ by making PS parallel to BH and PQ parallel to BC; let BD cut SP in T and CD cut PQ in R; take proportional segments Pr, Pt from PR,PT and let lines through the adjusted points concur at d (using Lemma XX); then d runs on the required trajectoria which is tangent at B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This parallelogram and proportional-segmentation method converts the four-points-plus-tangent constraint into the Lemma-XX product conditions and yields the desired conic pointwise by intersection procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXIV Prob. XVI — construct trajectoria through three points and two tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two tangents HI, KL and three points B,C,D: let BD meet the tangents at H,K and CD meet them at I,L; cut those secant constructions in R and S with proportional relationships given by geometric means (mean proportionals between segment pairs) to locate A and P the contact points; the two contact points provide the needed tangency data, from which the trajectoria is constructed as in previous problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mean-proportional constructions and tangency relations from conic theory (rectangles and squares proportionalities) to locate contact points; then proceed as in earlier propositions to draw the conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXII — transform figures into others of same genus preserving tangency/orders
rubrics_metrics.description: A general mapping: given a figure HGI and two parallel lines AO, BL intersecting a chosen transversal AB, one may map each point G of the original figure to a point g in a new figure hgi by constructing rays with prescribed angle and proportionality relations so that abscissas/ordinatas map by OA×AB/ad etc. Under this transformation tangents map to tangents, conic sections map to conic sections (circles included), and analytic curve order is preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this lemma to reduce difficult constructions by transforming the original figure into a simpler one (e.g., making converging lines parallel or turning a conic into a circle); after solving in the simpler figure, invert the transformation to obtain the solution in the original figure. The lemma guarantees preservation of tangency and analytic order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXV Prob. XVII — construct trajectoria through two points and three tangents (via transformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two points a,b and three tangents, use Lemma XXII to transform the figure so that two of the tangents become parallel and the third tangent becomes parallel to the line through a,b; in the transformed figure construct three contact points c,d,e by solving squared-rectangle proportionalities (as in the parallel case) and transfer them back to the original figure to obtain the trajectoria through the two points contacting the three given tangents. If the transformed positions place a,b between or outside the parallel tangents differently, the contact points must be chosen accordingly; if one of a,b lies between and the other outside, the problem is impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply an affine-like mapping to reduce the problem to a solvable parallel-tangents case, construct contact points by proportional/squared-rectangle relations, then invert the map. Watch the existence condition noted for placements of the given points relative to the tangents.
